To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have determined the half-lives for 20 nuclides, including those of the heaviest odd-odd particle stable nuclei Rh-90 to In-98, and have determined a large Gamow-Teller strength for the doubly magic Sn102.
we measured half-lives for 30 neutron deficient nuclei and observed fast beta-decay of odd-odd particle stable nuclei.
we have measured half-lives for 25 neutron-deficient nuclides and have observed fast beta-decay in the odd-odd nuclei Ag-94, In-98, and Tc-102.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the production, decay and identification of exotic nuclei far from the valley of stability.
the study of the decay properties of neutron deficient nuclei near the doubly magic nucleus Sn-102.
the production and study of exotic nuclei.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the decay properties of all nuclei in the region studied are well understood.
the decay of neutron deficient nuclei in the vicinity of Sn-100 is a very complex phenomenon.
the decay of the N approximate to Z nucleus is governed by the competition between the Gamov-Tiller, the Fermi and the internal conversion strength.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the decay properties of many new neutron-deficient nuclides were measured and the results were used to test nuclear models.
we have studied the beta-decays of many new nuclei and that we have measured the half-lifes for the first time in many cases.

we have measured the half-lifes of all known waiting point nuclides in the rp-process, we have observed for the first times fast superallowed Fermi decays in odd-odd particle stable nuclei, we have observed long-lived T = 1 states in the rp-process and we have determined the B-GT value for the decay Sn-102 -> In-102.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the beta-decays of the heaviest particle stable nuclei are dominated by superallowed Gamov-Teller transitions.
there is a large Gamov-Teller component in the beta-deay of Sn-102, which is consistent with a strong proton-neutron pairing in the ground state.
we have measured the half-lifetimes for 25 neutron-deficient nuclei, including the first measurements of the half-lives for the heaviest particle stable nuclei.
